title: Shigola — Tiles, Cache & Traces
description: Shigola: OGC API - Tiles. Two metric families that must never be summed together: shigola_cache_* (whole chain) and shigola_cache_tier_* (per tier). Built from the metric definitions in observability/prometheus, atlas/cache_collectors.go and provider/postgis.

panels.title: Overview
panels.description: shigola_cache_* is the whole chain (one hit = served from somewhere); shigola_cache_tier_* is per tier (several lookups per request). Never sum the two together.

panels.title: Request rate
panels.description: All routes, including the OGC landing page and /capabilities.

panels.title: Error ratio
panels.description: Non-2xx share of all responses. A 404 for a tile outside a layer's zoom range counts here.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio
panels.description: Whole-chain: served from any tier. Not the sum of per-tier hits.

panels.title: API latency p99
panels.description: Buckets are .25/.5/1/2.5/5/10s, so this is coarse — treat it as a band, not a number.

panels.title: Tier errors (range)
panels.description: A failing tier is logged, counted and skipped — reads degrade to a miss. No error status, no latency change. This counter is the ONLY evidence a tier is broken.

panels.title: API latency quantiles
panels.description: Coarse buckets (.25/.5/1/2.5/5/10s): every quantile below 250ms reads as 250ms.

panels.title: Top routes by request rate
panels.description: handler is the templated route. The native /maps/<map>/<layer>/{z}/{x}/{y} route is gone; tiles now appear as /collections/<collectionId>/tiles/<tileMatrixSetId>/<tileMatrix>/:tile_row/:tile_col.

panels.title: Response size quantiles
panels.description: Zero-dimensional by design — no per-route breakdown. Buckets: 500KB / 1MB / 5MB.

panels.title: Layer usage
panels.description: Demand keyed by OGC collection id: the bare <map> is a whole-map tile (one tile carrying every layer); <map>:<layer> is a single layer. Keyed on map AND layer, so two maps that both define a water layer stay separate series.

panels.title: Tile requests by layer
panels.description: Every cache get, hit or miss -- the closest thing to per-layer demand. Counts tile lookups, not HTTP requests.

panels.title: Share of tile requests
panels.description: Proportion of tile lookups over the range. The bare <map> slice is whole-map traffic, usually the majority.

panels.title: Tile lookups by layer (range)
panels.description: Absolute totals over the dashboard time range.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio by layer
panels.description: A layer with a low hit ratio and high volume is the one worth seeding.

targets.expr: label_replace(label_join(sum by (map_name, layer_name) (rate(shigola_cache_hits_total{map_name=~"$map", sub_command="get"}[$__rate_interval])) / clamp_min(sum by (map_name, layer_name) (rate(shigola_cache_hits_total{map_name=~"$map", sub_command="get"}[$__rate_interval])) + sum by (map_name, layer_name) (rate(shigola_cache_misses_total{map_name=~"$map", sub_command="get"}[$__rate_interval])), 1e-9), "layer", ":", "map_name", "layer_name"), "layer", "$1", "layer", "^(.*):$")

panels.title: Tile bytes served by layer
panels.description: Bandwidth attribution. A layer can be low-traffic but heavy.

panels.title: Layer demand by zoom
panels.description: Where each layer is actually being asked for. Steep growth at high z is the usual cache-sizing problem.

panels.title: HTTP tile request rate by collection
panels.description: Actual HTTP tile requests per collection. The bare <map> is a whole-map tile; <map>:<layer> is a single layer. Counts requests, not cache lookups, so a 404 is included here and absent from the panels above.

panels.title: HTTP tile latency p99 by collection
panels.description: Per-layer latency. Buckets are .25/.5/1/2.5/5/10s, so this is a coarse band. shigola_api_requests_total carries no handler label, so per-collection ERROR rate is not available -- only rate and latency.

panels.title: Cache — whole chain
panels.description: One hit here means the tile was served from somewhere in the chain.

panels.title: Cache latency p99 by op
panels.description: sub_command is get / set / purge.

panels.title: Cache errors & read timeouts
panels.description: Read timeouts are reads abandoned at the timeout_ms deadline. They are observed outside the deadline deliberately, so they still appear in the duration histogram.

panels.title: Cache — per tier
panels.description: Several lookups per request. Purges run in reverse tier order (durable first) to close the re-promotion race.

targets.expr: sum by (tier) (rate(shigola_cache_tier_hits_total{map_name=~"$map", tier=~"$tier"}[$__rate_interval])) / clamp_min(sum by (tier) (rate(shigola_cache_tier_hits_total{map_name=~"$map", tier=~"$tier"}[$__rate_interval])) + sum by (tier) (rate(shigola_cache_tier_misses_total{map_name=~"$map", tier=~"$tier"}[$__rate_interval])), 1e-9)
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, tier, sub_command) (rate(shigola_cache_tier_duration_seconds_bucket{map_name=~"$map", tier=~"$tier"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Tier errors
panels.description: THE tier health signal. A read failure is turned into a miss: the tile still serves, the status does not change and latency barely moves. If this is non-zero, a tier is broken.

panels.title: Tier read timeouts
panels.description: Reads abandoned at their timeout_ms deadline. Rising here usually precedes tier errors.

panels.title: Detached write pool
panels.description: Every cache writes off the response path through a bounded pool. The CLI cache worker and Lambda write inline instead, so neither shows up here.

panels.title: Write slots: in-flight vs capacity
panels.description: Alert on in-flight approaching capacity: drops only begin once the pool is already exhausted.

panels.title: Write outcomes
panels.description: timed_out is also counted in failed — do not add them. abandoned = still running when the shutdown drain deadline expired.

panels.title: Writes dropped
panels.description: Never attempted: pool full at admission.

panels.title: Writes timed out
panels.description: Killed by DetachedWriteTimeoutMs. Earliest warning the durable tier is degrading.

panels.title: Writes failed
panels.description: Attempted, returned an error. Includes the timed-out ones.

panels.title: Writes abandoned
panels.description: Still running at the shutdown drain deadline.

panels.title: Promotions
panels.description: Tiles promoted into an earlier tier after a lower-tier hit.

panels.title: Promotions dropped
panels.description: Promotions the write pool refused at admission.

panels.title: Mean detached write duration
panels.description: A mean only. For the tail read shigola_cache_tier_duration_seconds{sub_command="set"} instead.

panels.title: MVT SQL query latency
panels.description: mvtprovider/postgis — ST_AsMVT() server-side encoding.

panels.title: SQL query rate by provider
panels.description: Two families: mvtprovider returns encoded MVT from ST_AsMVT(); the standard provider returns features shigola encodes itself.

panels.title: Postgres pool usage
panels.description: Saturation here shows up as provider latency long before it shows up as errors.

panels.title: Traces (Tempo)
panels.description: All shigola spans carry the instrumentation scope github.com/MapColonies/shigola. A span whose error was a client disconnect is recorded as an event but NOT marked failed — the same line the prometheus observer draws.

panels.title: Slowest tile requests (>250ms)
panels.description: Server spans are named "<METHOD> <route>".

panels.title: Provider query spans (>100ms)
panels.description: Attributes: shigola.map, shigola.provider, shigola.layer_count, shigola.tile.z/x/y.

panels.title: Postgis query spans (>100ms)
panels.description: Carries db.query.text (truncated at MaxQueryTextBytes, flagged by shigola.db.query_truncated), db.system.name, server.address/port, db.namespace.

panels.title: Cache tier spans that missed
panels.description: shigola.cache.tier names the tier; shigola.cache.hit is the outcome.

panels.title: Spans with errors
panels.description: Status is set only when the failure is shigola's own. A client that disconnected mid-request fails everything in flight with its own context error; those spans record the error as an event but stay unset, so a busy service is not painted red for behaving correctly.

panels.title: Build info
panels.description: shigola_build_info — version, branch and commit from the ldflag targets in internal/build.
